name: abandoned rusted car facing south seen from above: trunk, roof and hood tops with cracked glass, front grille and bumper below
label: wasteland_ruins/car-rust-v

answer.evidence: The body is drawn as a stack of horizontal top planes: trunk (rows 1-8), roof (rows 11-21) and hood (rows 26-33), separated by glass bands that act as edge or eave lines (dark rows 9-10 and 24-25). Together they form about 34 rows of top surface. The hood ends in dark shadow rows 33-34, and below it a vertical front face of grille, headlights and bumper runs from rows 34 to 45, about 12 rows. The front face is clearly vertical and 3+ rows tall, so this is not a flat slab. The top planes read as a long foreshortened top. No receding side face is drawn. The silhouette stays 24-32 px wide.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a two-tile-wide car seen from above, drawn at the reference scale, so it is comparable to the stall and well. Measured facts are close to those references: 16 visible tones per tile against 17 for the stall and 20 for the well, 6% near-flat coverage against 13% for the stall, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted dark green-grey rather than black. This is not a sticker look. By eye, though, the body is mostly a few dull green-grey steps (about 4) with sparse rust speckle, a thin dark panel line, and a plain glass area with only a few crack pixels. The roof, hood and trunk read as broad, similar-valued panels. The grille and bumper are small, and the rust is not clustered or shaded the way the references' wood grain and per-stone shading are. The wheels and the lower front are also simple. It does not look thinner than the references on the numbers, but it is a little flatter and has fewer shading steps than the 5-6 of the well and stall. A careful artist would likely ask for more rust variation and highlight/shadow steps on the panels, and for more developed cracked glass. When in doubt, fail.
